page.guides.intro: Pick your client below. All settings use your full email address and mailbox password. Do not see your app listed? Only the clients on this page are supported.
page.guides.ios.s1: Open Settings > Apps > Mail > Mail Accounts > Add Account > Other > Add Mail Account; enter your name, full email address and password.
page.guides.ios.s2: Choose IMAP. Incoming server: box.urmail.cn, port 993, SSL on. Outgoing server: box.urmail.cn, port 587 with STARTTLS (or 465 with SSL). Username is always your full email address.
page.guides.ios.s3: Optional, for contacts and calendar: Settings > Apps > Contacts > Add Account (or Calendar) > Other, then add a CardDAV account and a CalDAV account with server box.urmail.cn and your email address and password.
page.guides.ios.s4: Optional, mail + contacts + calendar in one account: add an Exchange account with server https://box.urmail.cn/api/v1/mailbox/eas, leave Domain empty, username is your full email address. EAS availability is not publicly announced yet (see the note below).

page.guides.macos.s1: Open System Settings > Internet Accounts > Add Other Account > Mail Account and enter your full email address and password; macOS picks up IMAP (993 SSL) and SMTP (587 STARTTLS / 465 SSL) automatically.
page.guides.macos.s2: For contacts and calendar, add a CardDAV account and a CalDAV account in the same Internet Accounts panel, server box.urmail.cn, with your email address and password.

page.guides.thunderbird.note: Disclaimer: TbSync and the global databases approach are community projects, not part of Thunderbird itself. They work but are outside our support scope; sync problems there cannot be fixed by urMail.
page.guides.thunderbird.s1: Add a new mail account with your full email address; Thunderbird reads our autoconfig document (/mail/config-v1.1.xml) and fills in IMAP 993 SSL and SMTP 587/465 automatically. If it asks manually: IMAP box.urmail.cn 993 SSL, SMTP box.urmail.cn 587 STARTTLS.
page.guides.thunderbird.s2: Contacts and calendar: Thunderbird has no built-in CalDAV/CardDAV setup for arbitrary servers. Use the community TbSync extension with its Provider for Exchange ActiveSync / CalDAV & CardDAV, or connect via the Home Directory / global databases method.
page.guides.thunderbird.s3: Verify the account: send yourself a message and confirm it arrives on another device; then add the CardDAV address book URL https://box.urmail.cn/carddav/ if you connected contacts outside TbSync.

platform_backup_offsite.help: Configure an S3, SFTP, or WebDAV offsite backup destination. Credentials are encrypted with the platform master key and stored write-only (never returned). Saving replaces the whole destination. An unconfigured destination is an explicit disabled state, not an error.
platform_backup_offsite.load_failed: Failed to load offsite backup configuration
platform_backup_offsite.status.not_confi: No offsite destination configured (this is a normal state)
Until configured, backups stay local-only; once configured and enabled, every backup generation is synced offsite. Configure one below at any time.
platform_backup_offsite.type.label: Destination type
platform_backup_offsite.field.prefix_hin: Optional remote directory or object prefix.
platform_backup_offsite.field.endpoint_s: Optional (blank = AWS); custom endpoints must start with http(s)://
Required, host[:port] — no scheme, no path.
platform_backup_offsite.field.endpoint_w: Required, http(s)://host[:port] — embedded credentials are rejected.
platform_backup_offsite.field.age_recipi: An age encryption public key (starts with age1…) used for client-side encryption — a public key, not an email address.
platform_backup_offsite.field.enabled_hi: Credentials are required to enable: stored credentials or those entered now.
platform_backup_offsite.field.enabled_re: Disabling keeps the stored ciphertext — re-enabling does not require re-entering credentials.
platform_backup_offsite.credentials.reta: Leave credential fields blank to keep the stored credentials.
platform_backup_offsite.credentials.summ: Stored credentials cannot be decrypted (secrets subsystem problem) — re-enter credentials.
platform_backup_offsite.credentials.fiel: Region is required for S3 credentials (e.g. us-east-1).
SHA256:... format, pins the server host key; required for SFTP.
platform_backup_offsite.test.credentials: Credentials are required to test an unsaved destination.
platform_backup_offsite.error.invalid_pa: Invalid parameters (400 INVALID_PARAMS): bad field shape, length, or combination, or enabling without credentials.
platform_backup_offsite.error.secrets_un: Platform master key not ready (503 SECRETS_UNCONFIGURED): submitting credentials requires the secrets subsystem.
platform_backup_offsite.validation.requi: SFTP and WebDAV require an endpoint.
Region is required for S3 credentials.
S3 requires an access key ID.
S3 requires a secret access key.
SFTP requires a host key fingerprint (SHA256:...).
SFTP requires a password or a private key path.
platform_backup_offsite.validation.endpo: The S3 endpoint is empty or not a valid http(s) URL.
The SFTP endpoint must be host[:port] — no scheme, no path.
The WebDAV endpoint must be http(s)://host[:port] — no embedded credentials, no path.
platform_backup_offsite.validation.finge: The host key fingerprint must use the SHA256:... format.
platform_backup_offsite.validation.too_l: Field length limits exceeded (endpoint ≤300, bucket ≤255, prefix ≤300).

platform_backup_offsite.validation.crede: Enabling offsite backups requires credentials: enter them or keep the stored ones.
platform_backup_offsite.failure_semantic: If the destination is reachable but a later backup fails, the local backup still counts as successful; retention pauses until the next verified offsite copy; nothing offsite is ever deleted unless the latest generation has been verified there.
